transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

I’ve been thinking about death a lot and wondering if my family would be better off without me. I told my daughter about it when we were planning a trip, and she got so worried she brought me here to get help.
Have you had a similar episode of depression or feeling this way in the past, or is this the first time?

These heavy feelings aren't entirely brand new, but they've been coming and going for about a year now, especially since we started talking about my retirement. It has really ramped up and gotten much worse since I actually started cutting back my hours at work.
Did these symptoms start only after the retirement/work changes, or were you feeling depressed for a longer period before that as well?

It really started about a year ago when my husband and I first began seriously discussing my retirement. I wasn't feeling this way before those talks, but once we started planning to ease me out of work, these heavy moods began and then got much worse when I actually cut my hours.
Have you been feeling down or losing interest most days for at least two weeks at a time, even when the retirement/work changes are not on your mind?

Yes, I've felt completely flat and lost interest in everything I used to love, like hiking and the neighborhood festival, pretty much steadily for about a year now. It feels like a heavy, hopeless cloud that just won't go away, even when I'm not thinking about work or retirement. It's there almost every single day.
Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or making a plan to end your life?

Yes, I have. Every night when I lie down, I find myself thinking it would be easier if I just didn't wake up at all. I've even caught myself picturing ways to make that happen, just so my husband and kids wouldn't have to deal with me dragging them down anymore.
Have you thought about how you might act on these thoughts, or taken any steps to prepare?

I’ve pictured some ways I could make it happen, just in my head, thinking about how to end things so I'm not a burden anymore. But I haven't actually done anything to prepare or taken any physical steps to go through with it. It's just a heavy, constant thought when I'm lying in bed.
Did these symptoms begin only after a specific stressful event or life change, or have they been present for at least two weeks without a clear trigger?

They really started ramping up about a year ago when my husband and I began seriously discussing my retirement and I started cutting back my work hours. These dark, heavy spells and mood swings have been going on steadily for about a year now, which is much longer than just a couple of weeks.
Before the retirement changes started, did you have any depression or loss of interest lasting at least two weeks, or did these symptoms begin only after that stressor?

No, I didn't experience these kinds of prolonged, dark periods before we started talking about my retirement. Those heavy feelings and the loss of interest really only began about a year ago when my husband and I first had those serious discussions. While things have ramped up significantly since I actually cut my work hours, I was doing fine before we started planning for retirement.
Did this start after a specific stressful event or loss, and since then have you had symptoms like feeling constantly on edge, nightmares, flashbacks, or avoiding reminders of it?

While my mood struggles definitely began around the transition of planning my retirement and cutting back on work hours, I have not experienced nightmares, flashbacks, or any of those other symptoms. Those specific things aren't something I've been dealing with at all.
Have you been through a specific traumatic event or major stressful loss, and since then have you had symptoms like intrusive memories, nightmares, flashbacks, or avoiding reminders of it?
No, I haven't gone through any traumatic events or major losses like that. While retiring has been a very stressful transition for me, I don't have nightmares, flashbacks, or those kinds of symptoms.
Have your symptoms been tied mainly to the retirement/work change and improved when the stress is less, or have they stayed present most days regardless of what is happening in your life?

Even though it started with the retirement changes, these feelings haven't improved when the stress is low; they've stayed present almost every day. This heavy, hopeless depression has hung over me steadily for about a year now. Throughout this entire year, I've just kept swinging back and forth between being wound-up and sinking into these dark, heavy periods.
Have you had any period of at least two months during this past year when your mood and interest went back to normal, or has the depression been present almost continuously?

No, I haven't had any breaks like that. This heavy, hopeless depression has been present almost continuously for about a year now, ever since we first started talking about my retirement. I haven't had any periods where I felt back to normal during this past year.
Have you had any periods during this past year when you felt unusually energized, needed much less sleep, talked more than usual, or felt overly confident or restless?

Yes, I had a stretch a few weeks ago where I felt wired, touchy, and was talking a mile a minute. I had this sudden burst of energy where I was up before dawn reorganizing everything and felt like I was the only expert who could fix our condo community. My thoughts were racing so fast that it was incredibly hard to shut my brain off to sleep.
Have these energized periods lasted at least 4 days, and during them did you need much less sleep or do things that caused problems at work, at home, or with other people?

I’m not entirely sure how many days those periods lasted or how to answer the sleep part, though I definitely had a hard time shutting my brain off. I do know that I caused some worry with my family during those times, especially when my daughter had to talk me down from a risky financial decision.

Have you ever had a period of several days or more when you felt unusually energized or irritable with much less need for sleep, more talkative, racing thoughts, or risky behavior that was clearly different from your usual self?

Yes, I definitely had a stretch like that a few weeks back where I felt wired, irritable, and oddly upbeat out of nowhere, talking a mile a minute with racing thoughts. I was waking up before dawn to clean, reorganizing everything, and overcommitting to all kinds of volunteer projects. It was so unlike me that I even almost put a huge chunk of our savings into a risky housing project before my daughter talked me down.
During that energized period, did it last at least 1 week, or did it cause you to need hospitalization or seriously disrupt work, home life, or relationships?

No, that energized period only lasted for several days—less than a week—and I was never hospitalized. While I almost made that big mistake with our savings, the severe disruption to my daily life and work has really been driven by the heavy, dark periods. It's the overall toll of these unpredictable swings that has made me back away from everything.
During that energized period, did it last at least 4 days in a row, and was it clearly different from your usual self?

Yes, it lasted for about a week, so it was definitely at least four days, and it was completely different from my normal self. During that time, I was suddenly snapping at my husband over tiny things, talking a mile a minute, and constantly cleaning and organizing the house. It was like I was in a completely different gear and couldn't slow down.
Have you ever had a period like that that lasted at least 7 days, or was severe enough to require hospitalization or cause major problems at work, home, or in relationships?

Those "up" periods have happened as part of my swings over the past year, usually lasting several days at a time, but I have never been hospitalized for them. They did cause problems, though, like when I almost made a reckless decision with our savings before my daughter stopped me. These swings have really disrupted my life overall, making it hard to keep up with my work and family.
